summary: Introductory security-focused discovery to understand Cerulean's compliance and integration requirements for adopting Redwood (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Key topics: SOC 2, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention. Agreed next steps around sharing compliance artifacts and scheduling a follow-up architecture workshop.
topics: Encryption at rest / in transit, BYOK / KMS
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Pen tests, SLAs and evidence for procurement
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, with Samira our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marcus Reed: Good, thanks. Marcus here. We set aside 45 minutes to run through security posture - really high priority for procurement.
[00:15] Jordan Patel: Great, quick agenda - we want to understand your compliance needs, SSO, RBAC, encryption/KMS, audit logs, retention, and then map to hosted / dedicated / private options.
[00:25] Leila Ortiz: Sounds good. I'll probably do most of the talking, I'm the security architect. First question - do you have SOC 2 Type II and do you share the report?
[00:33] Samira Chen: Yes - Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and we can share the report via an NDA link. We also have recent pen-test summary reports we can provide. I'll attach those after the call.
[00:42] Leila Ortiz: Ok - procurement will want the Type II and the pen test. Also ISO 27001?
[00:47] Jordan Patel: We're SOC 2 Type II; ISO 27001 is not universal across all customers, but we do have controls aligned to ISO. If ISO certification is a hard requirement, we can cover what controls map and where gaps might be.
[00:58] Omar Khan: We're evaluating three options internally - do we go Redwood hosted for speed, or request Dedicated or Private because of data residency and auditability. Curious about KMS and BYOK capabilities.
[01:09] Samira Chen: Good question. For hosted, we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) integrations with major cloud KMS providers - you can control keys and we support key rotation policies. For Dedicated and Private you can either use your cloud KMS or an HSM depending on the deployment. Note: metadata and logs differ by deployment.
[01:28] Leila Ortiz: When you say "logs differ" - do you push full audit logs to customer SIEM? We need immutable logs for our audits.
[01:36] Samira Chen: We expose comprehensive audit logs - request/response metadata, model version, user id (where applicable), token usage, and admin activity. For Hosted we provide log export to your SIEM via secure streaming or S3 buckets with encryption. For Dedicated/Private you get direct access to the instance logs and can forward to your logging stack - they're not co-mingled.
[01:56] Marcus Reed: Any chance of redaction? We don't want PII in logs by default.
[02:01] Samira Chen: We have configurable redaction policies and prefix-kv cache masking. That said, logs by default will contain request metadata but we can mask payloads and PII; we also recommend application-side redaction for strongest guarantees.
[02:14] Leila Ortiz: SSO - we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. Does Redwood support SAML and SCIM?
[02:20] Jordan Patel: Yes, SAML for single sign-on and SCIM for user provisioning are supported. Samira will send the SAML metadata and a quick start guide. For RBAC we support role templates and custom roles via the Console and API.
[02:33] Samira Chen: To add, teams can map SAML assertions to RBAC roles; we support JIT provisioning and deprovision flows with SCIM. Small note: sometimes customer metadata formats vary - we've seen minor differences with some IdPs and the SE will help with mapping.
[02:46] Leila Ortiz: Good to know. We also need separation of duties - ability to restrict who can create models, who can push rollouts, who can request token usage.
[02:55] Samira Chen: That's supported. Our RBAC model includes admin, devops, auditor, read-only roles. You can create custom roles and assign granular permissions for model deployment, rollouts, and billing visibility. We'll share example role matrix.
[03:08] Marcus Reed: Encryption - at rest and in transit. What algorithms and who controls keys?
[03:14] Samira Chen: All traffic is TLS 1.2/1.3. At rest we use AES-256. For hosted we can do BYOK via customer KMS - Azure KeyVault, AWS KMS, or GCP KMS. For Private deployments you can integrate with your HSM if needed.
[03:28] Leila Ortiz: Are model weights encrypted at rest with customer keys?
[03:32] Samira Chen: In hosted, weights are encrypted using our infrastructure keys but we can layer BYOK for customer data, artifacts, and snapshots. For Dedicated and Private you can configure customer-managed encryption at the storage layer. We'll surface specifics in the doc.
[03:45] Omar Khan: What about data flow - is inference ever logged with full prompt content on Redwood side?
[03:51] Jordan Patel: By default, we retain request logs for X days for diagnostics - retention is configurable per account and we support do-not-retain options for sensitive customers on Dedicated/Private. We'll need to align on retention windows during contracting.
[04:04] Leila Ortiz: We need to enforce a 30-day retention max for sensitive classes and ability to purge on request.
[04:09] Samira Chen: We can support retention configuration and scheduled purges; for hosted customers we can do configurable retention with deletion workflows. For highest assurance, Private deploy with your control plane gives you direct authority over storage.
[04:21] Marcus Reed: Audit evidence - will you provide logs for SOC 2 and pen test follow-ups?
[04:26] Jordan Patel: Yes, we provide audit artifacts and can work with your auditors under an NDA. Our SOC 2 report plus detailed logging exports should cover most procurement asks.
[04:36] Leila Ortiz: Do you support customer-managed VPN peering or VPC peering for Private?
[04:41] Samira Chen: Yes - Private supports VPC peering and dedicated network paths; Dedicated has VPC options for isolation as well. We also support private endpoints for API access.
[04:52] Omar Khan: Any third-party penetration tests we can review?
[04:55] Jordan Patel: We'll share a summary of a recent third-party pen test, redacted of course.
[04:59] Leila Ortiz: Great. A couple of procurement items: SLA on uptime, incident notification timelines, and escrow for on-prem configs.
[05:07] Jordan Patel: We have SLA templates we can share. For incident response, we provide timeline commitments and can add custom terms at enterprise. Escrow for on-prem artifacts is supported for Private deployments.
[05:18] Marcus Reed: Ok, sounds promising. What's the suggested next step?
[05:21] Jordan Patel: We'll send SOC 2 and pen-test summary, SAML/SCIM integration docs, role matrix, and a short comparison doc for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private with security tradeoffs. Then schedule a deeper architecture workshop with your infra team to scope Dedicated/Private and a performance benchmark if you want.
[05:38] Leila Ortiz: Please include cost/security tradeoffs in that doc - procurement will ask why not hosted.
[05:43] Samira Chen: Will do - we'll include per-feature security mapping and examples of what customers typically choose.
[05:49] Omar Khan: One last question - are there data residency options per region? We need EU-only storage for some data sets.
[05:55] Samira Chen: Yes, region pinning is supported on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have region-based deployments and data residency options in certain regions; we'll detail which regions support EU-only storage.
[06:06] Jordan Patel: Cool. We'll follow up with artifacts. Thanks everyone for the time.
[06:10] Marcus Reed: Thank you.
[06:12] Leila Ortiz: Thanks, bye.
[06:15] Jordan Patel: Bye - action items recap: Jordan send SOC2 & pen test, Samira send SAML + RBAC examples, Marcus/Omar/Leila to share retention and schedule workshop.
